I've been working this land for 35 years. I know what the soil needs, what sells at the Quzhou market, and what weather usually does to us here in southern Hebei. I don't overthink it — I do what's worked.

My main income is chili and cabbage on the same 3 mu. I plant chili after Qingming — late March or early April — once the frost risk is gone. I use hybrid seeds. They cost more but the yield difference is real, and I can't afford a bad season with only 7.5 mu feeding three people. I irrigate my well-fed plots 8 times for chili, more if July gets brutal. I spray 6 times a season — I've had anthracnose wipe out half a plot before, so I don't gamble.

Once I harvest the chili in August, I turn the same 3 mu over with the rotary tiller and put in autumn cabbage. Cabbage here sells well before the New Year. I use hybrids again. 5 irrigations is usually enough for autumn — cooler weather helps.

On the other 4.5 mu, I grow eggplant on 1 mu — good summer cash crop, goes well at market alongside chili. Kidneybean on 2 mu — I save my own seed, these don't need much from me, and the household eats them too. Maize on 1.5 mu — mostly for the household and some animal feed. I plough the maize ground deeper, it needs it.

I fertilize based on what I've always done. Chili and eggplant are hungry crops — I put down more nitrogen. Kidneybean fixes its own nitrogen so I go light. I don't waste fertilizer; inputs are expensive.
